questions.stem: Using collision theory, why does increasing the concentration of a reactant in solution increase the rate?

options.text: The particles gain more energy and collide harder
The particles change orientation so more collisions are successful
There are more particles per unit volume, leading to more frequent collisions

questions.explanation: Increasing concentration means there are more reactant particles in the same volume of solution. The particles are closer together on average, so they collide more frequently. More collisions per second means more successful collisions per second, increasing the rate.
